Subject: Quick intro + migration goals

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro earlier — Priya and I had a chance to sync internally. We are exploring options to migrate large parts of our LLM usage off proprietary APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) to open-models/self-hosted runtimes to reduce vendor lock-in and unit cost. High level:

- Current: GPT-4.1 via OpenAI for generation, Claude for longer summarization flows, OpenAI embeddings for semantic search.
- Primary concerns: compatibility with existing prompt engineering (function calling + streaming), embeddings parity, inference latency for interactive flows, and security (SOC2 + VPC/KMS).

I've attached the RFP and a simple current-stack spreadsheet for reference. Would love a short follow-up call to go over tech requirements and potential POC. Are you available for 30 min on Monday or Tuesday?

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet you both earlier. Thanks for sending the RFP and stack sheet; I skimmed both and looped in Rishi (solutions engineer) and Aditya (security/compliance) so we can cover the technical and security parts on the follow-up.

I booked a 30-min slot for Monday 3/28 at 10:00am PT — invite sent. Goal for the call: confirm pain points, validate success criteria, and agree next steps (POC scope + timeline).

Quick summary of what I picked up from your note so we start aligned:
- Migration drivers: reduce per-token cost, remove lock-in, and improved control over data routing (VPC/KMS).
- Must-haves: function/tool-calling parity, streaming responses, embeddings compatibility (same vector dims / nearest-neighbor quality), and <1s 95th percentile latency for interactive flows.
- Nice-to-haves: dedicated GPU pools for spikes, model shortlist recommendations, and clear regression monitoring for quality.

On the call we'll go deeper into the prompt/response contracts you rely on (function signatures, streaming expectations) and confirm the eval set you'll want us to run for quality parity.

See you Monday — Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2027-03-28T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - Shoply

Alex / Priya — thanks for a productive call this morning. Per our discussion here is a short recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations.

1) Pain points we confirmed
- Cost: OpenAI/Anthropic spend is high and unpredictable at scale — Shoply is targeting ~40% unit cost reduction.
- Lock-in: Concerns about prompt/function compatibility and long-term dependence on closed APIs.
- Latency: Interactive flows (customer chat & agent assist) require sub-second responses at the 95th percentile.
- Security/compliance: Need SOC2 evidence, ability to run in a VPC with customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for requests.

2) Current stack (what you shared)
- Generation: OpenAI GPT-4.1 for assistant behaviors (few-shot / system prompts + function calls)
- Summarization: Anthropic Claude for multi-document summarization (batch jobs)
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings (1536-d) powering semantic search and rerank
- Orchestration: Internal microservice layer that handles prompt templating, function call wiring, and retries
- Hosting: AWS (us-west-2) with some batch jobs on GCP

3) Success criteria (agreed)
- Functional parity: function calling + streaming behavior must match existing contracts with minimal prompt changes.
- Quality parity: outputs within an agreed eval benchmark (we'll define a 200-prompt eval set).
- Latency: P95 < 1s for interactive flows under dedicated capacity assumptions.
- Cost: target ~40% reduction in token-based spend, measured over a 30-day test.
- Security: ability to run private deployment in a VPC with KMS and SOC2 evidence.

4) Compatibility requirements / technical constraints
- Function calling: must support structured function responses and stable JSON schemas; ability to stream partial function arguments while preserving schema validation.
- Streaming: chunked token streaming (server-sent events) and immediate mid-stream function invocation notifications used by your client.
- Embeddings: need 1536-d or compatible embedding vector; ability to support nearest-neighbor index (FAISS/Annoy) with same distance metric.
- Tokenization: prompt templates use standard BPE-style tokenization; minimal prompt rewrites preferred.

5) Initial model shortlist we discussed
- Redwood-7B-Quant (low-latency, good for assistant flows)
- Llama-2-13B / community fine-tuned variants (generation + function calling)
- MPT-7B-Instruct (good instruction-following, cheaper)
- A distilled 13B open-weight for summarization workloads (batch)

6) Proposed next steps & owners
- Redwood: (Rishi) run a technical deep-dive and confirm exact function-calling behavior, streaming contract, and an initial latency estimate for your payloads. Deliverable: tech-deep-dive doc + perf projection by 2027-04-04.
- Shoply: (Alex/Priya) share the 200-prompt eval set and any failing examples, and confirm the embedding evaluation queries. Deliverable: eval set by 2027-04-01.
- Redwood: (Aditya) start the security questionnaire prep and share SOC2/KMS architecture notes. Deliverable: initial security packet by 2027-04-05.
- Both: agree on POC scope (2-week POC: chat assistant + embedding migration) and commercial terms for a POC (trial credits / dedicated capacity).

7) Risks & open questions
- Prompt parity for complex function calls that rely on partial-streamed JSON — we'll need to validate against real client traces.
- Embedding vector parity — if exact dims differ we may need to re-index and run A/B on semantic quality.
- P95 latency target under realistic concurrency; we'll model this in the deep-dive.

8) Next meeting
- Tech deep-dive: 2027-04-04 (Rishi to lead)
- Kickoff POC (tentative): week of 2027-04-18 pending eval results and security sign-off.

Attachments referenced (from your send): Shoply_RFP.pdf, Shoply_current-stack-overview.xlsx

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please reply with edits. Otherwise we'll proceed with the owners/timestamps above.

Thanks again — excited to work together.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
